title: Product-measure criterion for the conditional special-pair law
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of the variable $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. Write $\mu$ for the conditional law, on the fiber $\{Z=z\}$, of the special bit-pair $(X_T,Y_T)\in\{0,1\}^2$, and write $\mu_X$ and $\mu_Y$ for the conditional laws on that same fiber of the individual special bits $X_T$ and $Y_T$. Suppose that for every pair $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$ the mass assigned by $\mu$ to the singleton $\{b\}$ equals the product $\mu_X(\{b_1\})\,\mu_Y(\{b_2\})$. Then $\mu$ is the product measure $\mu_X\otimes\mu_Y$.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic disjointness protocol p on inputs of length n
an achievable value z of the variable Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})
for every bit-pair b, the joint conditional mass on {b} factors as the product of the two marginal conditional masses on {b_1} and {b_2}
replaced: To prove the conditional special-pair law factors, it suffices to prove singleton factorization for the four bit-pairs.
